title: Listing security & communications playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for listing Redwood Inference products in cloud marketplaces (AWS, GCP, Azure) that focuses on: security acceptance criteria, customer-facing copy variants for compliance-conscious audiences, technical integration requirements, and internal communications templates. Use this as a pre-launch checklist and a short reference during vendor reviews.

Goals:
- Ensure every marketplace listing meets security/privacy requirements expected by enterprise buyers before publish.
- Keep copy consistent across marketplaces while offering compliance-first variants for regulated industries.
- Define a concrete go/no-go checklist that bridges GTM, Security, Legal, and Engineering.
- Provide comms templates for customers, partners, and internal teams on launch day and for rollback scenarios.

Quick summary of deliverables (minimum for launch):
1) Approved listing copy (short + long) and three compliance variants.
2) Security checklist signed off by InfoSec and SRE.
3) Billing/sku mapping doc for marketplace metering integration.
4) Support & escalation contact mapping and runbook snippet.
5) Launch comms (partner email, press-lite blurb, internal Slack + docs).

Acceptance criteria (must all be green):
- SOC2 Type II coverage documented for the hosting plan used by the listing (hosted or dedicated).
- Data handling blurb present on listing and matches private deployment options.
- KMS/HSM support described where applicable.
- Network boundaries & VPC integration notes included for Private offer types.
- Minimum SLAs and support tiers (response times) enumerated on the listing page.
- Billing SKU mapping tested with vendor sandbox (sample invoice validated).
- Automated observability hooks documented (what telemetry we expose to customers vs. what stays internal).
- Security scan report (static binary scan / dependency check) attached to PR.

Security & compliance checklist (operational):
- Ownership: InfoSec reviewer assigned (name + date).
- Artifact: Link to latest compliance evidence (SOC2 report, penetration test summary).
- Secrets: Confirm no hard-coded secrets in marketplace artifacts or example configs.
- Network: Define allowed IP ranges, VPC hooks, and egress rules for private offers.
- Key Management: Document how customer keys are used (bring-your-own KMS vs. Redwood-managed).
- Data locality: Specify regions qualified for regulated workloads and where logs are stored.
- Audit logs: Confirm audit-log retention options and whether exports to customer SIEM are supported.
- Vulnerability SLA: Agree on timelines for critical/important vulnerabilities discovery -> patch -> communicate.
- Third-party components: List third-party libs used by the listing (runtime, SDK) + license notes.

Technical/integration requirements (Engineering owners):
- Marketplace manifests: make sure manifest files (AMI/container image info, product description YAML) are finalized and stored in the listings repo.
- Metering hooks: Verify how usage will be tracked (per-token, per-embedding, per-request) and map to SKU IDs in vendor sandbox.
- IAM roles & service accounts: Provide minimal examples for customer setup (example policies for AWS IAM/GCP IAM roles).
- Deployment images: Publish images to agreed registries and tag with release candidate used by marketplace listing.
- Health checks: Implement and expose an /hc endpoint used by vendor for status checks (and document expected response).
- Security scanning: Ensure container images pass internal scanning pipelines (link to pipeline run ID).
- Rollback: Define the image/snapshot to roll back to, and how to revert listing metadata.

Copy guidance and short/long variants (Marketing / GTM):
- Tone: Focus on predictable performance, secure deployments, and cost controls for technical buyers. Keep short copy direct; long copy can include technical bullets and integrations.
- Short (hero): "Production-grade LLM inference — low latency, predictable cost, enterprise controls. Deploy hosted, dedicated, or privately."
- Long (detailed): "Redwood Inference provides a high-throughput runtime for modern LLMs with built-in batching, KV caching, and smart routing for predictable latency and unit cost. Choose hosted API for fast time-to-value, Dedicated pools for predictable throughput, or Private deployments for regulatory isolation. Integrates with your KMS and SIEM, supports canary rollouts, and includes observability and usage reporting suitable for enterprise procurement."
- Compliance-first variant (for regulated buyers): "Redwood Inference offers VPC and on-prem deployment options, customer-managed key support, SOC2 controls, and auditable logs — designed for healthcare, finance, and public sector workloads."
- Callouts (bullets to include on listing page):
  - SOC2-aligned controls; optional on-prem package
  - Per-token and per-embedding billing; SKU-ready for marketplace metering
  - Dedicated GPU pools and autoscaling policies with SLA-backed uptime
  - Integrates with customer KMS and standard SIEMs

Marketplace-specific notes (short checklist):
- AWS: Confirm AMI/CloudFormation/Service Catalog entries, marketplace metering SKU IDs, and AWS legal terms acceptance. Test purchase flow in AWS GovCloud if targeting US-Public Sector.
- GCP: Verify GCP Marketplace listing manifest and billing mapping. Validate container registry access for partner testing.
- Azure: Ensure managed application artifacts and terms are filled; check publisher verification state.

Support & escalation mapping:
- First line: Support docs + self-serve KB link on listing.
- Second line: Dedicated solutions engineering contact for onboarding; provide contact method and SLA.
- Critical incident: SRE on-call + GTM escalation contact; ensure actionable runbook is attached to marketplace PR.

Comms templates (copy snippets you can reuse):
- Partner email (short): "Hi <partner>, we’re publishing Redwood Inference to <Marketplace> on <date>. This listing supports dedicated/private deployment options and includes SOC2 evidence on request. Please review the partner portal entry here: <link>."
- Internal (Slack): "[#announce] Listing for Redwood Inference on <Marketplace> is scheduled for <date>. Highlights: SOC2 evidence available, metered billing mapped, and support runbook attached. PM: <owner>."
- Customer-facing FAQ snippet: "Is my data shared with the marketplace? No. Marketplace billing is used for purchase; your inference data and keys remain in your chosen deployment. See our data handling section for details."

Launch runbook (high level):
1) Final sign-offs: Legal, InfoSec, Product, Engineering.
2) Verify manifests and images in vendor sandbox -> perform end-to-end purchase + provisioning test.
3) Publish listing and monitor first 48 hours for errors/failed provisions.
4) Execute comms: partner email -> partner portal -> internal announce -> social/channel posts as approved.
5) Post-launch 7-day review: usage telemetry, support tickets, billing reconciliation.

Rollback triggers and actions:
- Trigger examples: failed provisioning >5% in first 100 purchases, critical security advisory affecting published artifact, billing mis-metering discovered.
- Immediate action: pause new purchases (if vendor console supports), retract listing versions if necessary, publish advisory to partners, trigger SRE incident.

Open questions and decisions needed (to track before final):
- Exact SKU mapping for per-embedding vs per-token — PM and Billing to finalize.
- Do we include a free trial credit offering on the listing or route trial to a separate promo flow?
- Which legal exhibit (terms addendum) do we attach for Private offers? Legal to provide template.

Owner & approvers:
- GTM owner: Maya Patel (owner)
- InfoSec reviewer: Ethan Li
- Engineering sign-off: Ben Carlson
- Legal reviewer: Sofia Ramirez

Next steps (immediate):
- PM to create JIRA epic that covers metering, manifests, and launch comms (link to JIRA-1183).
- Engineering to produce a sandbox end-to-end test and paste results into PR.
- InfoSec to attach latest SOC2 summary and fill the checklist above.

Notes / scratch area:
- Draft sample legal exhibit: "Marketplace offers do not change data ownership; Redwood acts as a service provider and will provide audit evidence upon request." (Legal to refine.)
- Example customer quote placeholder: "Redwood scaled inference for our search team from prototype to 25k qps with predictable cost per query."

-- end of playbook --

This document is intentionally iterative - treat as a living checklist. Drop comments below or ping owner on Slack for urgent edits.
